payload.definition_title: Bounded discrepancy relations — 有界差异关系 — 有界差の関係
payload.definition:
/- Adaptation draft: two complete original relation definitions and their two original notation commands. Mathematical bodies and context are unchanged. Original source notice retained. No source theorem or Open proof is imported. -/
/-
Copyright (c) 2026 Christian Merten. All rights reserved.
Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
Authors: Christian Merten
-/
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Defs
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

namespace AbcAdaptation.Reference


variable {α β : Type*}

/-- `DiscrepancyLE f g s`, denoted `f ≲[s] g`, means that `f` is bounded above by `g` up
to a bounded discrepancy on `s`, i.e. there exists a constant `C` such that
`f x ≤ g x + C` for all `x ∈ s`. -/
def DiscrepancyLE (f g : α → ℝ) (s : Set α) : Prop :=
  ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ s, f x ≤ g x + C

/-- `DiscrepancyEquiv f g s`, denoted `f ≈[s] g`, means that `f` and `g` agree up to a
bounded discrepancy on `s`, i.e. `|f x - g x|` is bounded on `s`. The equivalence classes
of this relation are called *BD-classes*. -/
def DiscrepancyEquiv (f g : α → ℝ) (s : Set α) : Prop :=
  DiscrepancyLE f g s ∧ DiscrepancyLE g f s

@[inherit_doc]
notation:50 f:51 " ≲[" s "] " g:51 => DiscrepancyLE f g s

@[inherit_doc]
notation:50 f:51 " ≈[" s "] " g:51 => DiscrepancyEquiv f g s

end AbcAdaptation.Reference
payload.natural_language_statement:
**Formal-code readback**

**English**

`AbcAdaptation.Reference.DiscrepancyLE`

**kind**

Definition of a proposition

**binders**

Implicit α : Type at an arbitrary universe level; explicit f,g : α → real numbers and s : Set α. The source also declares an implicit β : Type*, but β is unused and does not enter this definition.

**english**

There exists a real number C such that for every x of α, if x belongs to s, then f(x) ≤ g(x) + C.

**quantifier order**

[
  "Choose one C for the whole set s.",
  "For every x, and every proof that x belongs to s, the displayed inequality holds."
]

**qualifications**

[
  "C may depend on f, g, and s. It cannot depend on x.",
  "No positivity, normalization, finiteness, or nonemptiness condition is imposed on C or s."
]

**notation**

The expression f ≲[s] g abbreviates this proposition.

`AbcAdaptation.Reference.DiscrepancyEquiv`

**kind**

Definition of a proposition

**binders**

Implicit α : Type at an arbitrary universe level; explicit f,g : α → real numbers and s : Set α. The unused source variable β is absent.

**english**

DiscrepancyLE(f,g,s) and DiscrepancyLE(g,f,s) both hold.

**quantifier expansion**

There is a real C_forward such that every x in s satisfies f(x) ≤ g(x)+C_forward, and there is a real C_reverse such that every x in s satisfies g(x) ≤ f(x)+C_reverse.

**qualifications**

[
  "The two existential constants are independent.",
  "The definition does not state exact equality of f and g."
]

**notation**

The expression f ≈[s] g abbreviates this proposition.

**简体中文**

`AbcAdaptation.Reference.DiscrepancyLE`

隐式参数是任意宇宙层级中的类型 $\alpha$；显式参数为函数 $f,g:\alpha\to\mathbb R$ 和子集 $s\subseteq\alpha$。源码还声明了隐式类型变量 $\beta$，但它没有被使用，也不进入本定义。
本声明定义如下命题：存在实数 $C$，使得对每个 $x\in\alpha$，若 $x\in s$，则 $f(x)\le g(x)+C$。先为整个集合 $s$ 选择一个 $C$，再要求每个 $x$ 和其属于 $s$ 的每个证明均满足该不等式。$C$ 可以依赖 $f,g,s$，不能依赖 $x$。对 $C$ 或 $s$ 不施加正性、归一化、有限性或非空条件。记号 $f\lesssim[s]g$（代码写作 `f ≲[s] g`）缩写此命题。

`AbcAdaptation.Reference.DiscrepancyEquiv`

隐式参数是任意宇宙层级中的类型 $\alpha$；显式参数为函数 $f,g:\alpha\to\mathbb R$ 和子集 $s\subseteq\alpha$。源码中未使用的变量 $\beta$ 不属于本声明的参数。
本声明定义命题：`DiscrepancyLE(f,g,s)` 与 `DiscrepancyLE(g,f,s)` 同时成立。完全展开即：存在实数 $C_{\mathrm{forward}}$，使每个 $x\in s$ 满足 $f(x)\le g(x)+C_{\mathrm{forward}}$；并且存在实数 $C_{\mathrm{reverse}}$，使每个 $x\in s$ 满足 $g(x)\le f(x)+C_{\mathrm{reverse}}$。两个存在常数互相独立。定义不声称 $f,g$ 严格相等。记号 $f\approx[s]g$（代码写作 `f ≈[s] g`）缩写此命题。

**日本語**

`AbcAdaptation.Reference.DiscrepancyLE`

暗黙のパラメータは任意の宇宙レベルの型 $\alpha$、明示的パラメータは関数 $f,g:\alpha\to\mathbb R$ と部分集合 $s\subseteq\alpha$ である。ソースは暗黙の型変数 $\beta$ も宣言するが、これは未使用で本定義に含まれない。
宣言は次の命題を定義する。ある実数 $C$ が存在し、全ての $x\in\alpha$ について $x\in s$ ならば $f(x)\le g(x)+C$ となる。まず集合 $s$ 全体に一つの $C$ を選び、次に各 $x$ とその所属証明について不等式を要求する。$C$ は $f,g,s$ に依存してよいが、$x$ には依存できない。$C,s$ に正値性、正規化、有限性、非空性の条件はない。記号 $f\lesssim[s]g$（コードでは `f ≲[s] g`）はこの命題の略記である。

`AbcAdaptation.Reference.DiscrepancyEquiv`

暗黙のパラメータは任意の宇宙レベルの型 $\alpha$、明示的パラメータは関数 $f,g:\alpha\to\mathbb R$ と部分集合 $s\subseteq\alpha$ である。ソースの未使用変数 $\beta$ は本宣言のパラメータに含まれない。
宣言は `DiscrepancyLE(f,g,s)` と `DiscrepancyLE(g,f,s)` がともに成り立つという命題を定義する。展開すると、ある実数 $C_{\mathrm{forward}}$ が存在して全ての $x\in s$ で $f(x)\le g(x)+C_{\mathrm{forward}}$ となり、かつある実数 $C_{\mathrm{reverse}}$ が存在して全ての $x\in s$ で $g(x)\le f(x)+C_{\mathrm{reverse}}$ となる。二つの存在定数は独立である。$f,g$ の厳密な等号は主張しない。記号 $f\approx[s]g$（コードでは `f ≈[s] g`）はこの命題の略記である。

**Paper source context (English; separate from formal-code readback)**

DiscrepancyLE(f,g,s) means that some real C satisfies f(x)≤g(x)+C for every x in s. DiscrepancyEquiv(f,g,s) requires this bound in both directions. Thus the two functions differ by a bounded amount on s. The notation follows Mochizuki’s correction in IUT IV, Remark 2.3.1(ii), p. 55. Source notation: [GenEll], Definition 1.2(ii), p. 5, with the correction in IUT IV, Remark 2.3.1(ii), p. 55.

**Limits of the definition supplier**

The uncorrected direction printed in [GenEll], Definition 1.2(ii), p. 5 is reversed. Cite the correction when describing ≲.

The two directions may use different constants. A common absolute-value bound follows by taking their maximum.

These definitions introduce relations, not quotient types of BD-classes.

They apply to arbitrary real-valued functions on a type α. No geometric height theory is required to form the relations.

> The relation “$\approx$” clearly defines an equivalence relation on the set of functions $\mathcal F\to\mathbb R$; we shall refer to an equivalence class relative to this equivalence relation as a(n) [$\mathcal F$-]BD-class [i.e., “bounded discrepancy class”].

— Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position, §1, Definition 1.2(ii), sentences after the defining inequality, printed pp. 5.

> In [GenEll], Definition 1.2, (ii), the non-resp’d and first resp’d items in the display should be reversed! That is to say, the notation “$\alpha\lesssim_{\mathcal F}\beta$” corresponds to “$\alpha(x)-\beta(x)\leq C$”; the notation “$\alpha\gtrsim_{\mathcal F}\beta$” corresponds to “$\beta(x)-\alpha(x)\leq C$”.

— Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV: Log-volume Computations and Set-theoretic Foundations, §2, Remark 2.3.1(ii), correction of [GenEll], Definition 1.2(ii), printed pp. 55.

**Original papers**

[Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position](https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~motizuki/Arithmetic%20Elliptic%20Curves%20in%20General%20Position.pdf)

[Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory IV: Log-volume Computations and Set-theoretic Foundations](https://www.kurims.kyoto-u.ac.jp/~motizuki/Inter-universal%20Teichmuller%20Theory%20IV.pdf)
